A small prompt guide

Ask for the persona you need.

You don’t need to remember a special format. Describe the role and what you want done. These examples cover the common cases.

Start here

Use the first prompt for most new personas. Add an industry or context when it changes how the role works; otherwise the research uses a cross-industry default.

Recommended

Create and add a persona

Research the role, map its activities and workflows, then add it to the library.

Create a well-researched persona for a [role] in [industry or context] and add it to the Persona Library.

When you want to be explicit

Invoke the skill directly

Use this when you want to make sure the reusable research method is used.

Use $persona-research to create a persona for a [role]. Add it to the Persona Library.

Research only

Keep it out of the library

Get the research and synthesis without changing the live site.

Research the persona of a [role] in [context]. Give me the findings only; don’t update the Persona Library.

Extend an existing persona

Check another source

Give a URL or ask for a new source. The persona will be updated only where the evidence changes it.

Check another source for [persona name], summarize what it confirms, extends, qualifies, or contradicts, and add it to the Resources section.

What happens automatically

Ambiguity is scoped, not dumped on you.

If a role has multiple materially different interpretations, I’ll ask a short multiple-choice question with an Other option. Otherwise I’ll choose a sensible default and state it.

The role is mapped across the day.

Research is organized into activities, journeys, and workflows, with foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows separated when the evidence supports it.

Evidence stays visible.

New personas are marked Working draft until validated. Sources, confidence, open questions, and research limits remain visible.

Want to strengthen a persona?

Ask me to find or check a source. I’ll add the source trail, explain what it contributes, and revise only the affected claims or workflows.

The library workflow

ResearchUnderstand responsibilities, constraints, incentives, tools, and changing conditions.
ShapeTurn evidence into activities, journeys, workflow tiers, priorities, and a usable persona.
Keep currentCheck new sources later and update the evidence trail without rewriting everything.
